company_name: Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL), NSE: CDSL
business_description: CDSL is a securities depository. It holds investors' shares, bonds, mutual fund units and similar instruments in electronic (demat) form, records ownership, and processes transfers, corporate actions and IPO credits. It also provides e-voting, e-CAS statements and pledge / e-DIS services (FY26 Integrated Annual Report). Who buys: issuers (48,000+ issuers, 1.26 lakh ISINs) pay annual issuer charges; depository participants (585 brokers and banks) pay transaction and related charges; investors (18.01 crore demat accounts at 31 Mar 2026, about 80% market share) reach CDSL through those participants. Subsidiaries serve KYC registration/data customers (CDSL Ventures, CVL), insurance repository users (CIRL) and commodity repository users. Revenue split, FY26 consolidated revenue from operations Rs 1,144.92 Cr (FY26 audited results, filed 2 May 2026): Depository activity Rs 960.45 Cr (83.9%); Data entry and storage (CVL) Rs 182.81 Cr (16.0%); Repository Rs 3.41 Cr (0.3%); less inter-segment Rs 1.75 Cr. Within the standalone depository business (annual report): annual issuer charges Rs 456.38 Cr, transaction charges Rs 239.54 Cr, IPO / corporate action charges Rs 159.81 Cr; remaining operating streams about Rs 104.7 Cr (derived by subtraction from Rs 960.45 Cr). Q1 FY27 (audited results filed 1 Aug 2026): revenue Rs 292.76 Cr vs Rs 258.84 Cr (+13.1%); Depository activity Rs 246.70 Cr (+11.2%), Data entry and storage Rs 45.01 Cr (+21.8%), Repository Rs 1.27 Cr. Geography: no revenue split by geography is disclosed in the provided filings. The participant network is described as covering over 98% of India's PIN codes, and 84% of FY26 new accounts came from Tier II/III cities. A GIFT IFSC unit has SEBI clearance (annual report). Pricing power: the provided filings show no explicit tariff increase. Margins have compressed rather than held. Consolidated operating margin excluding other income (derived from audited results): 64.5% FY22, 54.7% FY23, 56.9% FY24, 53.2% FY25, 45.4% FY26; Q1 FY27 40.5% vs 44.5% in Q1 FY26. In Q1 FY27 total expenses rose about 21% against revenue growth of 13.1%.
moat_evidence: Intangible assets (licence / regulated status): the annual report describes CDSL as a securities depository with about 80% of demat accounts (18.01 crore accounts, 585 participants, 48,000+ issuers, 1.26 lakh ISINs at 31 Mar 2026). The filings provided do not quantify licence scarcity or name a competitor's share.

Intangible assets (persistent returns): consolidated return on owners' equity was 29.9% in FY25 and 23.3% in FY26, and operating margin excluding other income was 45.4% in FY26 (all derived from the audited FY25 and FY26 results). Returns are high but falling; the filings provide no named-peer margin comparison.
Intangible assets (proprietary data): the KYC subsidiary CVL holds about 10.33 crore KYC records and the depository dispatched about 31.7 crore e-CAS statements in FY26 (annual report).

Switching costs (participant integration): the annual report describes 80+ APIs and services such as e-DIS and margin pledge that brokers integrate with; 585 participants use the network. No participant churn figures are disclosed.

Switching costs (recurring issuer fees): annual issuer charges were Rs 456.38 Cr in FY26 (+40.2% from Rs 325.57 Cr in FY25; Rs 115.41 Cr in FY22), about 39.9% of FY26 consolidated revenue (annual report, audited results). The filings do not separate price from volume in this growth.

growth_driver_evidence.sales_marketing: No sales and marketing spend line was found in the provided filings. The nearest evidence is investor-education outreach: 3,600+ programmes reaching about 2 lakh participants and 130M+ YouTube views (FY26 annual report).
growth_driver_evidence.distribution_channels: Distribution runs through 585 depository participants and 80+ APIs, covering over 98% of India's PIN codes. The annual report carries testimonials from brokers including Angel One, Groww, Zerodha and Upstox. Accounts reached 18.01 crore at 31 Mar 2026 with about 2.71 crore added in FY26 (annual report).
growth_driver_evidence.geographic_expansion: GIFT IFSC unit with SEBI clearance, and CVL registered as a KYC agency in IFSC in Feb 2026 (annual report). Adjacent segments: insurance repository (about 22 lakh e-insurance accounts) and commodity repository (6,141 clients) per the annual report; the Repository segment earned Rs 1.27 Cr revenue with a Rs 1.40 Cr segment loss in Q1 FY27 (results filing). 84% of FY26 new accounts came from Tier II/III cities.
growth_driver_evidence.acquisitions: No acquisitions and no goodwill on the consolidated balance sheet. Small stakes only: Rs 1 Cr for 2% of Sahamati and Rs 5 Cr by the insurance repository subsidiary in RIX Systems (Q1 FY27 results notes); Rs 20 Cr invested in an associate, India International Bullion Holding IFSC, in FY25 and Rs 10 Cr in FY24 (cash flow statements). The associate recorded a share of loss of about Rs 4.1 Cr in FY26 versus a profit of about Rs 2.6 Cr in FY25 (cash flow adjustments), so value accretion is not yet shown.
growth_driver_evidence.pricing_power: Not disclosed in the provided filings as tariff changes. Indirect evidence is mixed: annual issuer charges rose 40.2% in FY26 while transaction charges fell 9.9% (Rs 265.94 Cr to Rs 239.54 Cr) and IPO / corporate action charges fell 1.2%; operating margin fell from 53.2% to 45.4%. The filings cannot separate price effects from volume.
growth_driver_evidence.new_products: The annual report lists recent launches and services including e-CAS statements (about 31.7 crore dispatched in FY26), Form 121 handling, demat account portability with closure automation, and proxy-advisor voting facilities. The provided filings do not give revenue by product for these, so their financial impact is not disclosed.
growth_driver_evidence.customer_retention: No churn or repeat-behaviour metric is disclosed in the provided filings. Supporting facts: about 80% share of demat accounts held (annual report), accounts of 18.01 crore, and annual issuer charges up 40.2% in FY26 to Rs 456.38 Cr.

risk_evidence.concentration: Not disclosed in the provided filings (no single-customer or top-N revenue share was found in the parts read). Context only: annual issuer charges come from 48,000+ issuers, while transaction and KYC-related fees are billed via 585 participants; concentration among those participants is not disclosed.
risk_evidence.disruption: The parts of the filings read describe no substitute for the core depository function. The KYC business (CVL, about 16% of FY26 revenue) is the segment where margins moved most: segment revenue +21.8% in Q1 FY27 but segment margin 23.4% vs 30.9% a year earlier (derived from the results filing). Technology expense rose 37.6% YoY in Q1 FY27 (Rs 47.64 Cr vs Rs 34.62 Cr), consistent with heavy technology investment. Any regulatory or industry KYC redesign is not discussed in the filings provided.
risk_evidence.outside_forces: Regulation: CDSL operates under SEBI regulation. The FY26 audited results note a pending arbitral award against CDSL (Anugrah matter, Bombay High Court) with no provision made and no amount quantified in the results notes. Market cycle: transaction charges fell 20.5% and IPO / corporate action charges fell 17.8% in FY23, and fell 9.9% and 1.2% in FY26, while total standalone income kept growing (annual report tables). Interest rates and markets: investments of Rs 727.7 Cr (current) and Rs 710.9 Cr (non-current) drive other income of Rs 93.6 Cr in FY26; fair-value gains inside that were about Rs 39.2 Cr in FY26 and Rs 68.4 Cr in FY25 (cash flow adjustments), and Q1 FY27 other income was Rs 47.74 Cr vs Rs 36.30 Cr. Forex, commodity input and tariff exposure: not disclosed as material in the parts read. Hedging: no borrowings and no hedging instruments were identified.
risk_evidence.competition: Not disclosed in the provided filings beyond the company's own market-share statement of about 80% of demat accounts (annual report). No competitor margin or competitive-intensity data was found in the filings provided.

price_sentiment_narrative: Not disclosed in the provided filings for the 12-month share price path or for analyst / institutional sentiment; no third-party views are used here. Bull arguments the filings support: Q1 FY27 revenue +13.1% with Depository activity +11.2% and Data entry and storage +21.8%; no borrowings, with Rs 727.7 Cr of current investments, Rs 710.9 Cr of non-current investments and Rs 51.4 Cr of cash at 31 Mar 2026; FY26 cash from operations Rs 466.62 Cr and free cash flow Rs 345.92 Cr; dividends paid of Rs 261.25 Cr in FY26. Bear arguments the filings support: FY26 revenue growth of only 5.8% and profit after tax down 13.5% (Rs 526.33 Cr to Rs 455.08 Cr); Q1 FY27 operating profit up only 3.0% (Rs 118.68 Cr vs Rs 115.25 Cr) against revenue up 13.1%, with about 78% of the rise in pre-tax profit coming from non-operating income; operating margin down from 53.2% (FY25) to 45.4% (FY26); trade receivables up 22.3% against revenue growth of 5.8%, and impairment on financial assets Rs 18.72 Cr in FY26 vs Rs 9.60 Cr in FY25; a Repository segment that is still loss-making; an unquantified arbitral award with no provision.

ai_risk_evidence.liability: The core product is the legal record of ownership for 18.01 crore demat accounts, and CDSL is SEBI-regulated. The FY26 audited results note a pending arbitral award against CDSL with no provision, which shows that record or participant failures can become legal claims. The provided filings do not describe human or physical oversight requirements, or any use of AI in the core product.
ai_risk_evidence.business_model: Based on reported FY26 consolidated revenue only, none of it is identified as per-seat or per-user. Annual issuer charges (39.9%) are an annual recurring fee per issuer. Volume or unit-linked streams are transaction charges (20.9%), KYC / data (16.0%) and IPO / corporate action charges (14.0%), together about 51% (derived), with about 9% in other operating streams.
ai_risk_evidence.physical_world: Predominantly software and digital records. Tangible assets are limited (net block Rs 461.71 Cr at 31 Mar 2026, mainly property and equipment) with no manufacturing. A small physical link exists through the commodity repository, which handles electronic warehouse receipts (6,141 clients per the annual report).
ai_risk_evidence.network: CDSL holds proprietary, non-public records: ownership data for 18.01 crore demat accounts and about 10.33 crore KYC records at CVL, plus about 31.7 crore e-CAS statements dispatched in FY26 (annual report). The filings do not say whether AI systems depend on this data or whether the company sells it, so external dependence is not disclosed.

bear.assumption: Revenue grows about 5% a year (FY26 grew 5.8%), EBITDA margin (excluding other income) slips to about 44% because expenses keep outgrowing revenue as in Q1 FY27, other income stays near Rs 90 Cr, and FY31 profit after tax is about Rs 478 Cr. The market pays 28x, below the company's recent range. The filings disclose no growth guidance, so this is analyst judgement anchored on FY26 and Q1 FY27 results.

base.assumption: Revenue grows about 12% a year (Q1 FY27 was +13.1%), EBITDA margin recovers to about 51% as expense growth slows toward revenue growth, other income of about Rs 125 Cr, tax about 25.5%, giving FY31 profit after tax of about Rs 756 Cr. Exit at 34x. No capacity or expansion plan is disclosed in the provided filings.

bull.assumption: Revenue grows about 16% a year on higher market activity, EBITDA margin rises to about 55% on operating leverage over a largely fixed technology platform, other income about Rs 150 Cr, giving FY31 profit after tax of about Rs 996 Cr. Exit at 40x.
